A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ECSEL and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. The retained material and additions can be reliably matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original symbolic-regression experiments, classification results on 11 datasets, and empirical shopping-intention and PaySim case studies, with additional results in Appendices D–G.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds non-signomial approximation experiments, matched-MLP comparisons, and empirical explanation-agreement and stability analyses.

M1.justification: The class-specific signomial model, sparsity-regularized objectives, probability transformations, and optimization procedures remain unchanged. Describing ECSEL as a network with exponential activations clarifies the existing architecture. Temperature scaling is suggested as a possibility, not introduced into the method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds eight non-signomial equations from AI Feynman and Nguyen, extending coverage to trigonometric, rational, and logarithmic target functions. This is a focused extension of the existing regression coverage; the 11 classification datasets and two application case studies are retained.

E2.justification: New Appendix E.5 evaluates matched per-class MLPs with raw and log-transformed inputs. The shopping comparison adds SVM and MLP, explicitly excluded in v1. Section 6.1 and Appendix F.5 additionally evaluate TreeSHAP, KernelSHAP, LinearSHAP, and LIME against ECSEL explanations, substantially expanding the actual comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include matched MLP capacity and input-representation controls, non-signomial fitting using 100 samples and best-performing K from {3,5,10}, and attribution-agreement and timing evaluations including 200 test instances. Existing classification splits and tuning protocols remain unchanged. The PaySim table caption changes MinMax scaling to StandardScaler, matching the existing prose without establishing that preprocessing was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of approximation under functional mismatch, the contribution of signomial parameterization versus matched MLPs, global explanation agreement, direct G3–LIME agreement, and LIME seed instability. The earlier polynomial-recovery failures, counterfactual illustrations, and sparse-versus-dense regularization study are retained; the regularization study is relocated.

E5.justification: v1 already specifies five symbolic-regression seeds and five-fold classification cross-validation. v2 newly reports classification CV means and standard deviations in Table 9, alongside Spearman significance tests, attribution-correlation dispersion, and a five-seed LIME stability analysis. These substantially expand statistical reporting without demonstrating an increase in the existing classification run count.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear in Tables 6, 11, 16, and 17, including non-signomial R2 values of 0.094 for Nguyen-5 and 0.9999 for Nguyen-7, and reported mean G3–LIME correlation of 0.997. Added SVM shopping recall of 76.57% exceeds the retained ECSEL value of 75.70%. Existing values also receive limited revisions: HEARTS LR summary accuracy changes from 80.33 to 81.97. The principal symbolic-recovery results and most existing classification scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The universal-approximation theorem, exponent-faithfulness proposition, interpretability properties, and proofs in Appendices A–C retain their mathematical substance and assumptions. Changes concern equation numbering, cross-references, and explanatory wording; relabeling Proposition B.1's proof does not add a proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, principal contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient signomial recovery, competitive classification, analytical interpretability, and application insights. Explicitly acknowledging established signomials and gradient optimization clarifies the novelty framing without changing the central claimed contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a calibration caveat, discusses approximation limits for oscillatory functions, hypothesizes inactive ReLU units as an explanation for matched-MLP failures, and contrasts neural-network weights with signomial elasticities. It also interprets explanation agreement and seed instability, discusses training-versus-explanation costs, and qualifies the shopping-recall comparison. These materially expand the mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: The code-release promise becomes a specific repository link reported as available. v2 adds matched-MLP configuration details, non-signomial sampling settings, shopping SVM/MLP thresholds, and an explanation of omitted LOAN results, including the MLP's 1049-second training time. Most existing implementation documentation remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Duffin and Peterson on signomial geometric programming, Guo et al. on calibration, and Tan et al. on LIME. It clarifies signomials as learned predictors rather than optimization objectives and relates ECSEL to shallow MLPs and explanation methods. Several other citation changes update bibliographic metadata for already-cited works.

P1.justification: The main narrative and Appendices A–G retain their organization. Local revisions expand related work, the illustrative example, and shopping-result discussion; add Appendix E.5; and move the regularization study into F.4. Front matter, acknowledgements, an impact statement, bibliographic formatting, and cross-references also change.

P2.justification: v2 introduces five tables, expands the classification summary with CV columns, and adds shopping comparator rows. It repositions existing tables and reformats the full classification results. Figures 1 and 2 are redrawn, while Figure 3d replaces the two-class display with annotated cancer-class bars. Figure 4 retains its original panels.

improvement.justification: The added architectural controls, classification uncertainty, explanation comparisons, and code-access information make the retained method easier to assess. However, some new conclusions exceed their evidence: Appendix E.5 claims higher accuracy and F1 on 10 of 11 datasets despite ties and lower TRANSFUSION F1 in Table 11, and Section 6.1 claims zero explanation cost despite Table 2 reporting 0.1 seconds. These issues limit the otherwise useful gains in empirical support and transparency.
